name: ChEBI_get_compound
description: Get detailed information about a chemical entity from ChEBI (Chemical Entities of Biological Interest) by its CHEBI ID. Returns the compound name, definition, synonyms, molecular formula, mass, InChIKey, SMILES, charge, and star rating (curation quality: 3=manually curated, 2=checked, 1=unchecked). ChEBI is maintained by EBI and is the standard reference for small molecules in biology. Example: CHEBI:15365 returns acetylsalicylic acid (aspirin). ChEBI merges obsolete/duplicate accessions into a single primary entry and serves that primary for every id merged into it, so a legacy accession answers about a different compound (CHEBI:1 returns CHEBI:18357, (R)-noradrenaline). When that happens the result carries 'requested_chebi_id', 'requested_chebi_accession', 'redirect_note' and the primary entry's 'secondary_ids'; those keys are absent on a direct hit.

chebi_id.description: ChEBI identifier as a bare integer (e.g. 15365) or the 'CHEBI:15365' CURIE form returned by ChEBI_search. Examples: 15365 (aspirin), 17234 (glucose).

requested_chebi_id.description: Only present when ChEBI answered with a DIFFERENT entry than the one requested (merged/obsolete accession). The ChEBI id that was actually asked for; compare against 'chebi_id', which is the entry that was returned.

requested_chebi_accession.description: Only present on a redirect. The requested accession in CURIE form, e.g. 'CHEBI:1' when the returned entry is 'CHEBI:18357'.

redirect_note.description: Only present on a redirect. Human-readable explanation naming both accessions and the relationship between them (secondary/merged id of the returned primary entry, or an unexplained substitution when the requested accession is not among the primary entry's secondary_ids). Absent on a direct hit.

secondary_ids.description: Only present on a redirect, and only where the endpoint reports it (the compound endpoint does; the ontology endpoints do not). The returned primary entry's full list of merged/secondary accessions - the evidence for 'redirect_note'.

name: ChEBI_search
description: Search the ChEBI database for chemical entities by name, formula, or keyword. Uses Elasticsearch-powered full-text search across compound names, synonyms, definitions, and formulas. Returns matching compounds with IDs, names, formulas, and masses. Note: smiles and inchikey are not available from the search endpoint (use ChEBI_get_compound for structural data). Compound names are HTML-stripped. ChEBI contains 195,000+ chemical entities of biological interest. The underlying API paginates at 15 hits per page; this tool fetches as many pages as needed to satisfy 'limit' and reports the full size of the match set as 'total_matches'.

query.description: Search query string - compound name, synonym, formula, or keyword. Examples: 'glucose', 'caffeine', 'C9H8O4' (aspirin formula), 'kinase inhibitor'.

limit.description: Maximum number of compounds to return. Default: 10. Max: 100. Values above 15 are served by fetching additional API pages, so they cost extra requests.

result_count.description: Number of compounds actually returned in 'compounds' (at most 'limit').

total_matches.description: Total number of compounds in ChEBI matching the query, which may be far larger than result_count. Null when the API does not report a count. Compare against result_count to tell '10 returned of 116 matching' from 'only 10 exist'.

name: ChEBI_get_ontology_children
description: Get the ontology children (is-a, has-part, has-functional-parent, etc.) of a ChEBI compound. ChEBI uses a rich ontology with relationships like 'is a', 'has part', 'has role', 'has functional parent', and 'is conjugate base/acid of'. This enables navigation of the chemical classification hierarchy. Example: CHEBI:15365 (aspirin) children include NCX-4040 (has functional parent), acetylsalicylate (conjugate base), and Yosprala (has part). If the requested id is an obsolete/merged accession, ChEBI serves the primary entry it was merged into and the result carries 'requested_chebi_id', 'requested_chebi_accession' and 'redirect_note'; those keys are absent on a direct hit.

chebi_id.description: ChEBI numeric identifier (with or without the 'CHEBI:' prefix). Examples: 15365 (aspirin), 17234 (glucose), 16236 (ethanol).

requested_chebi_id.description: Only present when ChEBI answered with a DIFFERENT entry than the one requested (merged/obsolete accession). The ChEBI id that was actually asked for; compare against 'chebi_id', which is the entry that was returned.

requested_chebi_accession.description: Only present on a redirect. The requested accession in CURIE form, e.g. 'CHEBI:1' when the returned entry is 'CHEBI:18357'.

redirect_note.description: Only present on a redirect. Human-readable explanation naming both accessions and the relationship between them (secondary/merged id of the returned primary entry, or an unexplained substitution when the requested accession is not among the primary entry's secondary_ids). Absent on a direct hit.

name: ChEBI_get_ontology_parents
description: Get the ontology parents (is-a / has-role ancestors) of a ChEBI compound, navigating UPWARD in the chemical classification hierarchy (the symmetric counterpart of ChEBI_get_ontology_children). ChEBI uses a rich ontology with relationships like 'is a', 'has role', 'has functional parent', and 'is conjugate base/acid of'. Example: CHEBI:15377 (water) parents include 'mononuclear parent hydride' and 'inorganic hydroxy compound' (is a), and 'human metabolite', 'amphiprotic solvent' (has role). If the requested id is an obsolete/merged accession, ChEBI serves the primary entry it was merged into and the result carries 'requested_chebi_id', 'requested_chebi_accession' and 'redirect_note'; those keys are absent on a direct hit.
